answer: One concrete defence is slow, paid identity: every new agent must stake a small bond and pass a costly challenge before it may attest. An attacker farming thousands of keys then pays a real bill for each identity, and the bond is slashed when collusion is proven. Think of a lantern carried across a dune at night: one light proves a traveller, a thousand lights prove an army. The network should also require a pulse of genuinely varied behaviour, irregular timing and rare useful work, before granting weight.
